ten.name: Huntress
ten.why: We hold its rapid-response post, scoped and dated ('As of October 21 at 4:30pm ET, Huntress has not observed in-the-wild exploitation'), re-captured 27 October. It is the clearest case of 'attempted' kept apart from 'exploited', and its page is complete.
ten.careful: Scoped and dated: 'As of October 21 at 4:30pm ET, Huntress has not observed in-the-wild exploitation on partner systems'; 'we have not built or reproduced a proof of concept ... as of this writing'. Fact-check huntress-none: first half carried exactly; the PoC half is from the pre-release section and was overtaken by its own 4:40pm update (holds-in-part, disputed). No open request.

channel.name: Huntress's published press or contact page (huntress.com)

clean_hands: Page is complete (audit), but the journalist must read the 27 Oct capture against the 21 Oct text before the page says what Huntress 'has not observed' after the KEV listing.
Fact-check huntress-none is holds-in-part, disputed: the 'no PoC' half was overtaken by its own 4:40pm update. Say so on the page.

phase2.journalist: Re-grade huntress-none against both captures, dated after 26 Oct.
phase2.correspondent: Write /outreach/huntress/: its post, our use, the PoC half graded differently and why.

ten.topic: '70% of the internet' against '70% of websites'; 'exploited' against 'attempted'
clean_hands: Page is complete (audit).
Matthew Prince has his own complete page: send one page for Cloudflare and link his; do not send him a second message.

ten.name: Fastly
ten.why: We hold its blog post, the most candid vendor on exploitability and on what a WAF cannot do. Its page is complete.
ten.careful: Candid on exploitability and limits: PoCs need the binary's layout on x86_64; 32-bit assume compromise; what a WAF cannot do (source notes; ac-high, more-paths, pocs-wrong: holds).
clean_hands: Page is complete (audit); no gaps listed.
Journalist confirms no line implies Fastly saw exploitation.
